words: الر تلك آيات الكتاب وقرآن مبين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening points to God's signs and the Qur'an's clear proofs, unseen matters, promises and threats that mutually confirm one another; their clarity makes threatened events as certain as witnessed facts, so 15:2 follows naturally.
rows.anchor: على أمرين واضحين : أحدهما ما نبه به سبحانه من الدلائل والآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their taunting impatience effectively asks for punishment to be hastened; God answers that every people has a fixed term, so He delays punishment without neglecting them and destroys them only when their appointed time arrives.
rows.anchor: فما من لحظة إلا وهي صالحة لأن يتوقع فيه العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw makes the fixed-term clause an added assertion; without it the clause would be bound to the preceding one like a necessary predicate or adjective. The written term is appointed in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: فأتى بالواو لأن الحال بدون الواو كالجزء من سابقها كالخبر والنعت الذي لا يتم المعنى بدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, when punishment comes at the time God wrote for them, they will learn whether they would then wish to submit.
rows.anchor: أو يكون التقدير : فسوف يعلمون إذا جاءهم العذاب في الأجل الذي كتبناه لهم

words: ما تسبق من أمة أجلها وما يستأخرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No community can precede its appointed term or delay it; the phrase clarifies that the preceding written book means each community's fixed deadline.
rows.anchor: ما يستأخرون * } أي عنه شيئا من الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural يستأخرون avoids a feminine singular تستأخر, which could be misconstrued as turning the statement into a direct address to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : تستأخر - حملا على اللفظ كالماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their passive wording reflects their denial of revelation itself; they name it mockingly, as if only Muhammad claimed it was sent down.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تكذيبهم بالتنزيل نفسه , بني للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Muhammad mad because he claims God sent him a Reminder, alleging that a jinn confuses him; their insult substitutes for an answer to the preceding argument and exposes their stubbornness.
rows.anchor: فكان هذا دليلا علة عنادهم , فإنهم أقاموا الشتم مقام الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand angels either to testify for Muhammad or to destroy opponents, and ask why he alone sees angels when he shares their humanity, lineage and homeland.
rows.anchor: دليلا على صدقك إما للشهادة لك وإما لإهلاك من خالفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand is baseless because decisive proofs already stand, foremost the Qur'an, which challenges them continually and demonstrates their inability to match it.
rows.anchor: بعد أن قامت على صدقه الأدلة القاطعة والبراهين الساطعة التي أعظمها القرآن الداعي لهم إلى المبارزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers their two demands by addressing the request for angels first because it is nearer in the discourse, then answers the charge against the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في قولهم أمران , أجاب عن كل منهما على طريق الاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend only for a true purpose: their message to prophets is truthful speech, while their action toward the warned is destruction or rescue.
rows.anchor: على الرسل فبالحق من الأقوال , وأما على المنذرين فبالحق من الأفعال من الهلاك والنجاة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains the angels' descent with truth as descent with the prophetic message and punishment.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : بالرسالة والعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If angels came at the unbelievers' request, judgment would immediately destroy the defiant rather than grant respite; delay also allows intended believers to be born from their descendants.
rows.anchor: فلو نزلوا عليهم كما اقترحوا لقضي الأمر بينك وبينهم فهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic We declares that God alone, not jinn or humans, sent down the Reminder gradually through Gabriel, answering the claim that a jinn confuses Muhammad.
rows.anchor: أي على ما لنا من العظمة لا غيرنا من جن ولا إنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the Reminder denotes both admonition and honor.
rows.anchor: أي الموعظة والشرف { وإنا له } أي بعظمتنا وإن رغمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves the Reminder perpetually through His power and knowledge; its divine preservation rules out its being the confused speech of a madman.
rows.anchor: أي دائما , بقدرتنا وعلمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's sound reason, high resolve, certainty, precision, trustworthy judgment and firmness likewise contradict the charge of madness.
rows.anchor: يعلمون أنك أكملهم عقلا , وأعلاهم همة , وأيقنهم فكرا , وأتقنهم أمرا

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports Zayd's account that after Yamama's heavy losses among Qur'an reciters, Umar persuaded Abu Bakr to commission Zayd to gather the Qur'an from written materials and people's memories; Zayd found al-Tawba's closing verses only with Khuzaima, or Abu Khuzaima, al-Ansari.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري في التفسير والفتن عن زيد بين ثابت رضي الله عنه قال : أرسل إلي أبو بكر

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd's report says the compiled sheets remained with Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Hafsa, showing their custody after the first collection.
rows.anchor: وكانت الصحف التي جمع فيها القرآن عند أبي بكر حتى توفاه الله تعالى ثم عند عمر حتى توفاه الله

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that Hudhayfa feared divergent recitations among Syrian and Iraqi forces; Uthman borrowed Hafsa's sheets and tasked Zayd, Ibn al-Zubayr, Sa'id b. al-As, and Abd al-Rahman b. al-Harith to copy, use Quraysh dialect for disputes and burn other copies.
rows.anchor: وروي بعده عن أنس رضي الله عنه أن حذيفة بن اليمان رضي الله عنه قدم على عثمان

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd reports that a verse of al-Ahzab he often heard the Prophet recite was missing from the collected codices and found only with Khuzaima, whose testimony counted as that of two men.
rows.anchor: وله عن خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت أنه سمع زيد بن ثابت رضي الله عنه قال : لما نسخنا الصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jann is the race of jinn, with Adam standing to humans as its counterpart; another view identifies al-jann as Iblis.
rows.anchor: والجان } أي الذي هو للجن كآدم عليه السلام للناس : وقيل : هو إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added preposition conveys how briefly and closely the jinn's creation preceded the human creation.
rows.anchor: وعبر عن تقليل زمان سبق خلقه وتقريبه بإثبات الجار فقال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samum is intensely hot fire.
rows.anchor: نار السموم * } أي الحر الشديدن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An anonymous report describes smokeless samum fire as the source of lightning, positioned between heaven and the veil; when God wills, it pierces the veil and falls where commanded, and the heard thunder is that breach.
rows.anchor: قيل : هي نار لا دخان لها , يكون منها الصواعق , وهي بين السماء وبين الحجاب

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi describes samum as a subtle fire boiling intensely in the atmosphere, compared with ordinary fire as ice is to water and stone to soil.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي في اللوامع : نار لطيفة تناهت في الغليان في أفق الهواء

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah says samum is one seventieth of the fire from which jinn were created; its name reflects its subtle penetration through bodily pores, as poison does.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله : هذه السموم جزء من سبعين جزءا من السموم التي خلق الله منها الجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation itself should suffice to direct worship to the Creator, but the misguided ignored it; God's greater favor of distinguishing humans among creatures also reveals the cause of their deviation and honors Muhammad through Adam.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت نعمة الإيجاد كافية في إخلاص العبادة للموجد , ثم لم يعتبرها أهل الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is a creature with human form and unblemished skin; صلصال is very dry clay, حمأ is black stinking mud, and مسنون describes Adam's shape in hollows and limbs as if molded.
rows.anchor: من صلصال } أي طين شديد اليبس { من حمإ } أي طين أسود منتن { مسنون * } أي مصور بصورة الآدمي

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani derives مسنون from continuing along one direction, as in على سنن واحد.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : وأصله الاستمرار في جهة من قولهم : على سنن واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command recalls God's speech to the angels, honoring Muhammad by honoring his father Adam.
rows.anchor: أي واذكر قول ربك إذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's fashioning means completing and adjusting Adam, preparing him almost fully for the imparting of spirit.
rows.anchor: أي عدلته وأتممته وهيأته لنفخ الروح تهيئة قريبة من الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breathing the spirit means creating life in Adam, figuratively like fire catching in a wick through blowing; attributing the spirit to God honors it, and its highest excellence is making a knower act humbly.
rows.anchor: أي خلقت الحياة فيه كما تعلق النار بالفتيلة بالنفخ , وهو تمثيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels were commanded to prostrate in honor of Adam; falling as if involuntarily conveys their immediate and easy obedience.
rows.anchor: اسجدوا له سجود من كان في مبادرته به وسهولة انقياده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All angels prostrated when the command came for Adam, their human forefather, while his descendants were still in his loins.
rows.anchor: أي بسبب هذا الأمر من غير توقف لما جاء الوقت الذي أمرتهم فيه لذلك البشر

words: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even one divine blessing has innumerable branches, so people cannot count or encompass God's favors despite ingratitude and rejection of reminders; gratitude would bring more bounty.
rows.anchor: أي كلكم { نعمة الله } أي إنعام الملك الذي لا رب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps pouring out blessings because He is forgiving and merciful, although people's neglect and heedlessness would otherwise make them deserve loss.
rows.anchor: فلذلك هو يدر عليكم نعمه وأنتم منهمكون فيما يوجب نقمه

words: والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything hidden and public; this makes the duty of gratitude and ugliness of disbelief plain, while idols know nothing, making their worshippers foolish.
rows.anchor: ليعلم مقدار المضاعفة لموجبات الشكر وقباحة الكفر , وأما الأصنام فلا تعلم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are worshipped idols.
rows.anchor: أي دعاء عبادة { من دون الله } أي الذي له جميع صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone has perfect power, knowledge and creation; idols cannot create anything and are themselves created, so they cannot be divine.
rows.anchor: ولما أثبت لنفسه تعالى كمال القدرة وتمام العلم وأنه المنفرد بالخلق , شرع يقيم الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are truly lifeless, further removed from divinity than merely lacking power and knowledge; even a living creature that must eventually die cannot be God.
rows.anchor: قال نافيا عنها الحياة - بعد أن نفى القدرة والعلم - المستلزم لأن يكون عبدتها أشرف منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because jinn may speak from idols and report stolen-hearing that proves true, the text does not deny every awareness; it denies knowing resurrection's time, about which their reports are false.
rows.anchor: لم ينف عنها مطلق العلم , بل نفي ما لا علم لأحد غيرالله به , لأنهم لا يخبرون عنه بخبر إلا بان كذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negating perception, which is broader than knowledge, rules out every more specific kind of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فنفي عنهم مطلق الشعور الذي هو أعم من العلم , فينتفي كل ما هو أخص منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here دخلا means corruption, scheming, disease or deception in dealings; the intensified form suggests a sound nature strongly resists this deliberate misconduct.
rows.anchor: أي فسادا ومكرا وداء وخديعة { بينكم } أي في داخل عقولكم وأجسامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fraudulent oaths make a previously firm foot slip from its place in religion or worldly standing, leaving no security and causing a fall; Arabs use this image for trouble after safety.
rows.anchor: { فتزل } أي فيكون ذلك سببا لأن تزل { قدم } هي في غاية العظمة بسبب الثبات

words: وتذوقوا السوء بما صددتم عن سبيل الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who use corrupt oaths to hide truth taste evil for barring themselves and others from God's path; the harm continues while they persist, and dying in that state brings lasting punishment.
rows.anchor: { بما صددتم } أي أنفسكم ومنعتم غيركم بأيمانكم التي أردتم بها الإفساد لإخفاء الحق

words: ولا تشتروا بعهد الله ثمنا قليلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not trade God's covenant for worldly possessions, which remain a trifling price even when people regard them as valuable.
rows.anchor: أي تكلفوا أنفسكم لجاجا وتركا للنظر في العواقب

words: إنما عند الله هو خير لكم إن كنتم تعلمون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward in both abodes is better; only a stubborn person of deficient judgment exchanges it, and the condition challenges people to truly know rather than act like beasts.
rows.anchor: ولا يعدل عن الخير إلى ما دونه إلا لجوج ناقص العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant encompasses oaths: this passage begins the sequence by commanding fidelity and ends it by forbidding breach, with specific oaths between for emphasis.
rows.anchor: فصار العهد الشامل للأيمان مبدوءا في هذه الآيات بالأمر بالوفاء به ومختوما بالنهي عن نقضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people possess is transient worldly goods they naturally pursue; it runs out, distressing the owner when lost or causing anxiety about its loss.
rows.anchor: أي من أعراض الدنيا , وهو الذي تتعاطونه بطباعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reward endures and will be given to those who remain steadfast in His covenant; this promise also hints at the hardship patience requires.
rows.anchor: أي الذي له الأمر كله من الثواب { باق } فليؤتينكم منه إن ثبتم على عهده

rows.speaker: الجماعة، ابن كثير، عاصم
rows.claim: The majority read ولنجزين with third-person yāʾ, while Ibn Kathir and Asim read it with majestic first-person nūn, a shift to direct divine speech.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجماعة بالياء ونحن - على قراءة ابن كثير وعاصم بالنون التفاتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who patiently fulfill God's pleasing commands and avoid prohibitions receive their reward; God's generosity raises lesser deeds to the level of the best deeds.
rows.anchor: على الوفاء بما يرضيه من الأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards according to the best deeds, raising all works to that level and making lesser works equal to the best.
rows.anchor: أخبر بأنه يعمد إلى الأحسن فيرفع الكل إليه ويسوي الأدون به

words: من عمل صالحا من ذكر أو أنثى وهو مؤمن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise applies equally to any believer, male or female, who does righteous work; faith is the condition completing the general wording.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت عامة , وكانت ربما خصت الذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pleasant worldly life means steadfastness and purity of character; greater faith brings trials, which do not negate happiness.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا بما نؤتيه من ثبات القدم , وطهارة الشيم

words: ولنجزينهم أجرهم بأحسن ما كانوا يعملون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers receive their full reward in this world and the next according to their best deeds, so trials do not imply lost felicity.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا والآخرة { بأحسن ما كانوا }

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars say the obedient live comfortably whether wealthy or poor: the poor have contentment, while sinners are discontented and even wealthy sinners remain restless through greed.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء رضي الله عنهم : المطيع في عيشه هنيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Qur'an joins recitation, reflection and action, its guidance calls for seeking refuge from Satan so whispers cannot block understanding or corrupt good works; this urges reflection, sincerity and diligence, especially in heart's actions, and addresses Muhammad to teach others a fortiori.
rows.anchor: تسبب عن ذلك الأمر بأنه إذا قرئ هذا القرآن المنزل على مثل تلك الأساليب الفائقة يستعاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not let one who disbelieves in the Hour turn you from remembering it and preparing; worldly adornment stirs rivalry and fills hearts with pride and boasting.
rows.anchor: أي إدامة ذكرها ليثمر التشمير في الاستعداد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Moses' dignity, the warning against unbelief is phrased as a ban on an unbeliever turning him aside; the cause implies the danger of disbelief, while a successful deterrent signals slackness in faith.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من العبارة نهي موسى عليه السلام عن التكذيب , فعبر عنه بنهي من لا يؤمن عن الصد إجلالا لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses must stand firm even against a multitude: their numbers appeal to desire, not proof. The passage urges evidence over blind imitation and warns that ruin accompanies imitators, as al-Kashshaf notes.
rows.anchor: وإنذار بأن الهلاك والردى مع التقليد وأهله نبه عليه الكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever follows desire with all effort, becoming like an irrational beast; that condition is repellent and leads to ruin.
rows.anchor: أي بغاية جهده { هواه } فكان حاله حال البهائم التي لا عقل لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتردى means perish: one moment of neglecting divine watchfulness leads away from evidence, and deviation from evidence leads to destruction.
rows.anchor: أي فتهلك , إشارة إلى أن من ترك المراقبة لحظة حاد عن الدليل , ومن حاد عن الدليل هلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though God knows the answer, He gently asks about the exalted object in Moses' right hand to reassure him and establish a sign of the Hour through the swift transformation of his known staff.
rows.anchor: مريدا - بعد تأنيسه بسؤاله عما هو أعلم به منه - إقامة البينة لديه بما يكون دليلا على الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is invited to look closely at his familiar staff as it becomes a living creature, strengthening conviction and confirming those to whom he will be sent.
rows.anchor: بقلب العصا حية بعد تحقق أنها عصاه يقرب النظر إليها عند السؤال عنها ليزداد بذلك ثباتا ويثبت من يرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers that it is his staff, outwardly and inwardly.
rows.anchor: أي ظاهرا وباطنا { عصاي } ثم وصل به مستأنسا بلذيذ المخاطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says he leans on and relies on it when tired or needing help over slips, descents, climbs, leaps, darkness and similar situations.
rows.anchor: أي أعتمد وأرتفق وأتمكن { عليها } أي إذا أعييت أو أعرض لي ما يحوجني إلى ذلك من زلق أو هبوط أو صعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After listing how the staff serves his own needs, Moses turns next to the needs of his flock.
rows.anchor: ثم ثنى بعد مصلحة نفسه بأمر رعيته فقال
